authorityBoundary.operatorAuth: One process-wide bearer protects all non-public non-internal routes; there are no per-route operator roles, fresh confirmation or four-eyes approval.
authorityBoundary.serviceAuth: Internal connector and shadow routes use scoped Ed25519 Relay identity with bounded request bodies and replay state.
authorityBoundary.currentExecutionBoundary: KairosEngine._execute_candidate_locked unconditionally records HOLD and returns before the retained legacy submit implementation.
authorityBoundary.legacySubmitImplementation: Retained _legacy_execute_candidate_locked plus IOC order/read-back/reconciliation code is not called by the mounted entrypoint, but remains in the deployed process image.

criticalFindings: The hard HOLD makes current order submission unreachable through the observed mounted application even if live flags, credentials and a candidate are present.

The same broad operator bearer can start/stop the autonomous worker, mutate runtime limits and set both KAIROS_LIVE_TRADING and the literal confirmation value; these changes are applied to process environment immediately.
The worker asks the committee and LUMI only as advisory, records the verdict, then ignores it before execution; timeout, error, HOLD or FREEZE therefore supplies no accepted veto.

The deployed process still contains create_order and multi-leg submit code. Removing the unconditional HOLD or accidentally mounting the legacy router would restore money-writing authority without persisted immutable intents or idempotent claims.

The retained two-leg submit launches orders concurrently; a one-leg success plus exception can be ambiguous before durable intent/attempt evidence, and the exception path does not prove provider reconciliation before future retry.

Operator state, memory and ledger are mutable host files rather than an accepted transactional source of truth; current state writes are not crash-durable and ledger entries are not an immutable hash-chained execution journal.

limitations: Static deployed-source inspection proves current call-graph reachability, not that future edits or an alternate entrypoint cannot expose retained legacy execution.
Only public health and an unauthenticated 401 fence were called; no operator state, configured flags, account balances, credentials or provider endpoints were queried.
No worker start/stop, limit change, committee evaluation, exchange call, order submit, deploy, restart or configuration mutation was performed.

independentReviews.finding: All mounted and background callers terminate at the unconditional HOLD; dormant legacy submit remains unsafe to re-enable without persisted intents, idempotent attempts and ambiguous-submit recovery.
